rules.statement: When code chooses a value from several sources (an explicit override, a parsed file, a default fallback), add a test for each branch, including a test that the explicit override wins over the parsed value, not just a test of the fallback.
rules.why: If only the fallback is tested, a regression that always returns the default, or an override that gets ignored, would still pass the suite.
rules.check: For new or changed value-resolution logic with an override parameter, a parsed source and a default, check that the tests cover the parsed non-default value, the fallback, and the override taking precedence.

rules.statement: When code enforces a limit such as a search depth, maximum size or count, add a test case just past the limit that checks the input is ignored or rejected, not only cases inside the limit.
rules.why: Tests that stay inside the limit don't notice if the limit is widened or removed.
rules.check: For a diff that adds or changes a limit (for example `-Depth`, a max length), look for a test with input beyond the limit that asserts it is excluded.

rules.statement: Don't ask a script that is shipped and run on its own to import a helper shared with other scripts; a small duplicated parse is acceptable when a comment names the script it mirrors and a test pins the behavior.
rules.why: A standalone script that is copied alone into consumers, or that hands off to a newer copy of itself, can't depend on a sibling module. And the other copy may be a generated file that can't be edited directly.
rules.check: Before reporting duplicated logic between scripts, check whether one script is distributed or run standalone, or whether the other copy is generated, and whether a comment names the mirrored script. If so, don't report it.
